items.title: Bob Lovett Interview, 1949-04-01
items.q: I remember I was impressed by Rapolo. I liked him. In fact, I remember I used to play his solo on the Tin Roof Blues

ctx.x: G-E-R-O-U-L-D. By that time they had become also called the South Side groups. They had made many of these recordings in Chicago. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yeah. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. They were the New Orleans men. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Now, many of the early Chicagoans had listened to the original Dixieland Jazz Band, then later to the New Orleans Rhythm Kings. At any time do you remember those coming into your observation?

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yes, the New Orleans Rhythm Kings I remember we listened to. And yes, I remember I was impressed by Rapolo. I liked him. In fact, I remember I used to play his solo on the Tin Roof Blues, and I was very proud of the fact that I could play that.
G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Was there an effort to emulate his tone and effects as well as just the phrase?
